rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God dispersed the Israelites across the earth, placing each group in a region so few regions lacked them; this completed their humiliation and left them without collective strength.
rows.anchor: فرقنا بني إسرائيل أو صيرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispersal is one of the Qurʾān’s reports of the unseen, like the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: وهذا من مغيبات القرآن كالذي تضمنته الآية قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Communities” may be the second object of “We dispersed” or a circumstantial accusative describing the dispersed Israelites.
rows.anchor: إما مفعول ثان لقطعنا وإما حال من مفعوله منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The righteous” may be a subject with a fronted, omitted predicate, or the agent of the adverbial phrase; the clause can describe the communities or function circumstantially.
rows.anchor: والصالحون مبتدأ وجوز أن يكون فاعلا للظرف

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari identifies the righteous as those who believed in God and His Messenger and remained steadfast before Jesus was sent.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري من آمن بالله تعالى ورسوله وثبت على دينه قبل بعث عيسى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid are credited with the view that the righteous were those who lived to meet the Prophet and believed in him.
rows.anchor: هم الذين أدركوا النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وآمنوا به ونسب ذلك إلى ابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view places the righteous Israelites beyond China; al-Ālūsī also locates them there.
rows.anchor: هم الذين وراء الصين وهو عندي وراء الصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those below the righteous fall short of their rank: they believe but obey some commands and violate others.
rows.anchor: منحطون عن أولئك الصالحين غير بالغين منزلتهم في الصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take “below that” to mean the Israelites who disbelieved, if “righteousness” here means faith; another view includes both unbelievers and sinners.
rows.anchor: هم الكفرة منهم بناء على أن المراد بالصلاح الإيمان

rows.speaker: الطبرسي وأبو الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī treats “below” as a subject left in the adverbial form; Abū al-Ḥasan compares its retained fatḥa to “between you” in 6:94.
rows.anchor: على ماذكره الطبرسي مبتدأ إلا أنه بقي مفتوحا لتمكنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A noun described by an adverb or clause is regularly omitted when it is part of a noun governed by preceding min or fī; an additional proposed parsing is unsound.
rows.anchor: ومن المشهور عند النحاة أن الموصوف بظرف أو جملة يطرد حذفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point of the wording is to divide the Israelites into two groups.
rows.anchor: ومحط الفائدة الانقسام إلى أن هؤلاء منقسمون إلى قسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular demonstrative can refer to the plural righteous; alternatively, it points to righteousness itself, with “people of” understood.
rows.anchor: الإشارة للصالحين وقد ذكروا أن اسم الإشارة الفرد قد يستعمل للمثنى والمجموع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good things are fertility and well-being; the bad things are drought and hardship.
rows.anchor: الخصب والعافية ( والسيئات ( الجدب والشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trials are meant to bring them to repent of what they had been forbidden to do.
rows.anchor: أي يتوبون عما كانوا عليه مما نهوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse confirms the preceding point that the idols do not follow their worshippers’ calls.
rows.anchor: تقرير لما قبله من عدم إتباعهم لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Calling” may mean worship, naming the idols as gods, or invoking them; in the worship and naming readings, the two objects are omitted.
rows.anchor: والدعاء إما بمعنى العبادة تسمية لها بجزئها أو بمعنى التسمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted objects mean either that they worship the idols besides God or that they name them gods besides Him.
rows.anchor: أو تسمونهم آلهة من دونه سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols, like their worshippers, are owned by God, subject to His command, and incapable of benefit or harm.
rows.anchor: مملوكة لله تعالى مسخرة لأمره عاجزة عن النفع والضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the idols are even more visibly powerless, likening them to their worshippers confronts people who admit their own weakness yet claim idols can act.
rows.anchor: مع كون عجزها عنهما أظهر وأقوى من عجزهم إنما هو لاعترافهم بعجز أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possibility is that carved human-shaped idols are treated hypothetically as living, rational beings like their makers, yet still unworthy of worship.
rows.anchor: لما نحتوا الأصنام بصور الأناسي قال سبحانه لهم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads inna with a light n and ʿibādan in the accusative.
rows.anchor: قرأ سعيد بن جبير ( إن الذين تدعون ) بتخفيف إن ونصب عبادا أمثالكم

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī parses the light form as a negative إن functioning like the Hijazi mā, an analysis associated with al-Kisāʾī and some Kufans.
rows.anchor: وخرجها ابن جني على أن إن نافية عملت عمل ما الحجازية وهو مذهب الكسائي وبعض الكوفيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Critics object that this negative construction is unattested and appears to deny the likeness asserted by the familiar reading.
rows.anchor: واعترض أولا بأنه لم يثبت مثل ذلك وثانيا بأنه يقتضي نفي كونهم عبادا أمثالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The replies say the construction occurs in Arabic; the readings need not conflict because one can affirm likeness in one respect while the other denies it wholly or in another respect.
rows.anchor: وعن الثاني أنه لا تناقض لأن المشهورة تثبت المثلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing treats the light إن as a weakened heavy إن that unusually governs both accusatives; because this is rare and weak, some leave إن ungoverned and supply an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: إنها إن المخففة من المثقلة وإنها على لغة من نصب بها الجزئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A recited heavy anna has ʿibādan as a circumstantial accusative from the omitted pronoun and amthālukum as its nominative predicate.
rows.anchor: بالتشديد و ( عبادا ) بالنصب على أنه حال من العائد المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further transmitted form has amthālukum nominative with the light reading and ʿibād accusative, parsed as a circumstantial accusative plus predicate.
rows.anchor: في قراءة التخفيف ونصب ( عباد ) وخرج ذلك على الحالية والخبرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is a taunting challenge: call on the idols to remove harm or bring benefit if the worshippers are truthful.
rows.anchor: تحقيق لمضمون ما قبله بتعجيزهم وتبكيتهم أي فادعوهم في رفع ضرأ وجلب نفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge concerns the worshippers’ claim that their idols can do what the worshippers themselves cannot.
rows.anchor: قادرون على ما أنتم عاجزون عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions intensify the rebuke by showing the idols lack the faculties needed to answer the preceding challenge.
rows.anchor: تبكيت إثر تبكيت مؤكد لما يفيده الأمر التعجيزي من عدم الإستجابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If likeness means actual equality, idols are inferior to humans, making their worship even less fitting; if likeness is hypothetical, the verse cancels that supposition.
rows.anchor: في المماثلة كر على المثلية بالنقض لأنهم أدون منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the light, negative reading of inna, these questions further establish the idols’ incapacity and lack of likeness.
rows.anchor: وعلى قراءة التخفيف وإرادة النفي تقرير لنفي المماثلة بإثبات القصور والنقصان

words: أَلَهُمْ أَرْجُلٌ يَمْشُونَ بِهَآ أَمْ لَهُمْ أَيْدٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each of the four faculties is questioned separately to repeat the rebuke and show that absence of any one suffices to disprove the ability to answer.
rows.anchor: ووجه الإنكار إلى كل واحد من تلك الآلآت الأربع على حدة تكريرا للبكيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point is simply incapacity, not that possessing limbs is a condition of divinity; the verse does not deny God’s divinity or establish the corporealism claimed by some anthropomorphists.
rows.anchor: وليس المراد أن من لم يكن له هذه لا يستحق الألوهية وإنما يستحقها من كانت له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording makes the leg’s function the target: since the idols show none of the characteristic action of real legs, they are not legs in reality; the same applies to the other organs.
rows.anchor: ووصفه الأرجل بالمشي بها للإيذان بأن مدار الإنكار هو الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Am is disconnected here; its hamza continues the rebuke, while bal shifts from one completed mode of argument to another.
rows.anchor: منقطعة وما فيها من الهمزة لما مر من البكيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-baṭsh means taking hold with force.
rows.anchor: والبطش الأخذ بقوة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads yaṭbishūn with ḍamma on ṭāʾ, a dialectal form meaning to take what they want or defend you.
rows.anchor: بضم الطاء وهو لغة فيه

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: The hands follow the legs because walking describes the idols’ condition in themselves, whereas grasping describes their relation to others.
rows.anchor: كما قال شيخ الإسلام لما أن المشي حالهم في أنفسهم والبطش حالهم بالنسبة إلى الغير

words: أَمْ لَهُمْ أَيْدٍۢ يَبْطِشُونَ بِهَآ أَمْ لَهُمْ أَعْيُنٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hands precede eyes and ears to pair with legs and because lack of walking or grasping is more obvious and more forceful as a rebuke.
rows.anchor: ولأن انتفاء المشي والبطش أظهر والبكيت به أقوى

words: أَمْ لَهُمْ أَعْيُنٌۭ يُبْصِرُونَ بِهَآ أَمْ لَهُمْ ءَاذَانٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eyes precede ears because they are more familiar and more evident in appearance and effect; seeing by eyes and hearing by ears are ordinary outward associations.
rows.anchor: فلأنها أشهر منها وأظهر عينا وأثرا وكون الإبصار بالعين والسماع بالأذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse supports the view that God places in some things a power by which they have effects when He permits; al-Ālūsī rejects calling this near disbelief.
rows.anchor: أودع في بعض الأشياء قوة بها تؤثر إذا أذن الله تعالى لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to confront the idolaters and renew the challenge after establishing that their partners can do nothing.
rows.anchor: أمر له صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بأن يناصبهم المحاجة ويكرر عليهم البكيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He challenges the idolaters and their partners to devise every possible plot against him without delay, expressing complete fearlessness.
rows.anchor: شركاءكم واستعينوا بهم علي ( ثم كيدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two first-person yāʾs are omitted in the written form; Abū ʿAmr retains the yāʾ of kaydūn at connection, Hishām in both positions, and other readers omit it. In 11:55 all retain it in kaydūnī; al-Ajhūrī says tunẓirūnī always omits its yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وياء المتكلم في الفعلين مما لم يثبتوها خطا وقرأ أبو عمرو بإثبات ياء كيدون وصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those “near your Lord” are the angels of the highest assembly; nearness means rank and divine favor, not place, since God is transcendent.
rows.anchor: وهم ملائكة الملأ الأعلى فالمراد من العندية القرب من الله تعالى بالزلفى والرضا لا المكانية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes “near your Lord” to mean near the Lord’s Throne.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد عند عرش ربك لايستكبرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels perform worship as they have been commanded.
rows.anchor: لايستكبرون عن عبادته ( بل يؤدونها حسبما أمروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their glorification declares God utterly free of whatever does not befit His majestic presence.
rows.anchor: ينزهونه عما لا يليق بحضرة كبريائه على أبلغ وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They devote ultimate servitude and humility to God alone and associate no one with Him.
rows.anchor: ويخصونه بغاية العبودية والتذلل لا يشركون به غيره جل شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fronted “to Him” indirectly reproaches other morally responsible beings who fail to worship as the angels do.
rows.anchor: كما يدل عليه تقديم ( له )

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭībī reads the whole statement as a rationale: worship sincerely as commanded, since God has honored servants and needs neither people nor their worship; fronting also serves the verse ending.
rows.anchor: كما آثره العلامة الطيبي لأنه تعليل للسابق على معنى ائتوا بالعبادة على وجه الإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prostration at this verse may follow a commanded prostration, oppose unbelievers’ refusal, or imitate prophets’ prostration; this instance fits the latter two explanations through allusion or explicit mention.
rows.anchor: وقد جاء الأمر بالسجدة لآية أمر فيها بالسجود امتثالا للأمر أو حكى فيها إستنكاف الكفرة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports a Prophetic supplication in prostration asking God for beneficial knowledge and deeds that raise one’s rank.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر اللهم لك سجد سوادي وبك آمن فؤادي اللهم ارزقني علما ينفعني

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet repeatedly said during night recitation prostrations, “My face prostrates to its Creator”; the Tirmidhī report is graded authentic by al-Tirmidhī.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وأبو داود والترمذي وصححه عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that each Muslim prostration raises a degree, removes a sin, or grants both.
rows.anchor: وجاء عنها أيضا ما من مسلم سجد لله تعالى سجدة إلا رفعه الله تعالى بها درجة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that Satan weeps when Adam’s child prostrates and gains Paradise, while Satan refused and faces the Fire.
rows.anchor: وأخرج مسلم وابن ماجة والبيهقي عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī infers that quiet remembrance is preferable and supports this with Aḥmad’s report, “The best remembrance is silent.”
rows.anchor: استدل بالآية على أن إخفاء الذكر أفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He condemns the religiously, rationally, and conventionally objectionable practices of ignorant Sufis of his time.
rows.anchor: وهي ناعية على جهلة زماننا من المتصوفة ما يفعلونه مما يستقبح شرعا وعقلا وعرفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, the single soul is the spirit and its mate is the heart; the spirit inclines and rests toward the heart, sensing subtle graces from it.
rows.anchor: وهي الروح ( وخلق منها زوجها ) وهي القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Covering” signifies spiritual union; Sufis hold that this union runs through all created things, as in 67:3.
rows.anchor: أي جامعها وهو إشارة إلى النكاح الروحاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light burden represents the first faint appearance of human attributes in the spiritual heart; its later heaviness represents the growth of those attributes and fear of losing spiritual qualities to carnal ones.
rows.anchor: في البداية بظهور أدنى أثر من آثار الصفات البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit and heart call on God because they fear luminous spiritual qualities will be replaced by dark, lower qualities.
rows.anchor: لأنهما خافا من تبدل الصفات الروحانية النورانية بالصفات النفسانية الظلمانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask for something fit for servitude and promise gratitude.
rows.anchor: لئن آتيتنا صالحا ) للعبودية ( لنكونن من الشاكرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good granted to them represents faculties given according to their innate disposition.
rows.anchor: صالحا ) بحسب الفطرة من القوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their descendants attribute partners to God in what He provides them; some become servants of appetite, clothing, or money.
rows.anchor: أي جعل أولادهما لله تعالى شركاء فيما آتى أولادهما فمنهم عبد البطن ومنهم عبد الخميصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this reading, whatever is invoked besides God shares human incapacity and has no independent effect.
rows.anchor: في العجز وعدم التأثير ( فادعوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks the worshippers to call their alleged partners about any matter and test whether they truly attribute efficacy to them.
rows.anchor: فليستجيبوا لكم إن كنتم صادقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question denies that idols have legs to walk; God alone makes them walk, and the same interpretation applies to the other faculties.
rows.anchor: استفهام على سبيل الإنكار أي ليس لهم أرجل يمشون بها بل الله عز وجل إذ هو الذي يمشيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward challenge tells opponents to plot against the Prophet if they can, continuing the exposure of their alleged powerlessness.
rows.anchor: إن إستطعتم ( إن وليي الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the Prophet’s guardian and caretaker; He sent the Book and cares for the righteous, understood as those who uphold it steadfastly.
rows.anchor: حافظي ومتولي أمري ( الذي نزل الكتاب وهو يتولى الصالحين

words: وَتَرَىٰهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ وَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers appear to look but do not perceive truth or the Prophet’s reality because their hearts are blind.
rows.anchor: الحق ولا حقيقتك لأنهم عمي القلوب في الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Take what is easy and accessible for people rather than imposing what is difficult.
rows.anchor: خذ العفو ) أي السهل الذي يتيسر لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Enjoin what is recognized” means enjoin the beautiful and gracious way.
rows.anchor: وأمر بالعرف ) أي بالوجه الجميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turn away from the ignorant instead of repaying their ignorance in kind.
rows.anchor: الجاهلين ) فلا تكافئهم بجهلهم

words: خُذِ ٱلْعَفْوَ وَأْمُرْ بِٱلْعُرْفِ وَأَعْرِضْ عَنِ ٱلْجَٰهِلِينَ
rows.speaker: جعفر الصادق
rows.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq says no Qurʾānic verse gathers the excellences of character more comprehensively than this one.
rows.anchor: عن جعفر الصادق رضي الله تعالى عنه ليس في القرآن آية أجمع لمكارم الأخلاق من هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says the verse’s strong implication of divine oneness makes the believer gentle: seeing God’s control over people’s actions, one does not quarrel, overburden, or grow angry in command and prohibition.
rows.anchor: قيل وذلك لقوة دلالتها على التوحيد فإن من شاهد مالك النواصي وتصرفه في عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge means witnessing God’s presence and recognizing that no one besides Him acts; this alludes to anger and its remedy.
rows.anchor: بالشهود والحضور فإنك ترى حينئذ أن لا فعل لغيره سبحانه وهذا إشارة إلى ما يعتري الإنسان أحيانا من الغضب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say anger arises when one condemns another’s action while seeing oneself as capable and the other as helpless.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : إن الغضب إنما يهيج بالإنسان إذا إستقبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A flash of rational light reveals that God created the offender’s motive and that the eternal decree preceded it, changing anger; knowing God’s secret in destiny makes calamities easier, and refuge seeks this insight.
rows.anchor: عرف أن المغضوب عليه إنما أقدم على ذلك العمل لأن الله تعالى خلق فيه داعية وقد سبقت عليه الكلمة الأزلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward gloss takes piety here as avoiding associationism.
rows.anchor: إذا مسهم طائف من الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A satanic touch is the attribution of an act to someone other than God; remembering oneness restores the vision that God is the only agent.
rows.anchor: لمة منه بنسبة الفعل إلى غيره سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “brothers” are Satan’s veiled companions.
rows.anchor: إخوان الشياطين من المحجوبين ( يمدونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satanic companions prolong people in error by attributing agency to other-than-God, while remaining obstinate in disputation.
rows.anchor: الشياطين في الغي وهو نسبة الفعل إلى السوي ( ثم لا يقصرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Why did you not produce it?” means: why did you not gather or fabricate the sign on your own initiative?
rows.anchor: لولا اجتبيتها ) أي جمعتها من تلقاء نفسك

words: قُلْ إِنَّمَآ أَتَّبِعُ مَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَىَّ مِن رَّبِّى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet follows only revelation because he stands by it, not by himself.
rows.anchor: ما يوحى إلي من ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one reading, listen to the Qurʾān with outward ears and be silent with the inward senses.
rows.anchor: أي القرآن بآذانكم الظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “listen to it” may refer instead to God: He is the speaker addressing people through the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: إذا قريء القرآن فاستمعوا للرب جل شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy may come through true hearing or through the manifestation of the Speaker’s qualities and acts in His speech.
rows.anchor: بالسمع الحقيقي أو برحمة تجلي المتكلم في كلامه بصفاته وأفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God inwardly may mean adorning oneself with whatever divine qualities one can take on, or following the Prophet as the model in 33:21.
rows.anchor: بأن تتحلى بما يمكن التحلي به من صفات الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humility and awe vary according to the spiritual station.
rows.anchor: تضرعا وخيفة ) حسب اختلاف المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remember inwardly without making the remembrance publicly audible.
rows.anchor: ودون الجهر ) أي دون أن يظهر ذلك منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mornings” signify the appearance of the spirit’s light, while “evenings” signify the dominance of the soul’s qualities.
rows.anchor: أي وقت ظهور نور الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means never to be heedless of witnessing essential unity.
rows.anchor: ولا تكن ) في وقت من الأوقات

words: وَٱذْكُر رَّبَّكَ فِى نَفْسِكَ تَضَرُّعًۭا وَخِيفَةًۭ
rows.speaker: بعض الأكابر
rows.claim: Some spiritual masters assign inward, humble remembrance to those who have arrived at witnessing; quiet remembrance to travelers toward it; and vigilance to lower-ranking novices.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الأكابر : إن قوله سبحانه وتعالى : ( واذكر ربك في نفسك تضرعا وخيفة ) إشارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear signals awe of divine majesty; the cited poem says the speaker lowers his gaze from reverence, not fear, to protect beauty.
rows.anchor: أشتاقه فإذا بدا أطرقت من إجلاله لا خيفة بل هيبة وصيانة لجماله

rows.speaker: السهروردي
rows.claim: Al-Suhrawardī says the beginner’s or traveler’s method depends on the shaykh, a heart physician who may prescribe vocal remembrance to interrupt distracting thoughts.
rows.anchor: وفي عوارف المعارف للسهروردي قدس سره لا يزال العبد يردد هذه الكلمة على لسانه

rows.speaker: السهروردي
rows.claim: Al-Suhrawardī describes repeating the dhikr aloud with the heart accompanying it until it displaces inner speech; when the heart absorbs it, remembrance becomes witnessing, unveiling, and direct vision, the aim of retreat.
rows.anchor: حتى تصير متأصلة فيه مزيلة لحديث النفس وينوب معناها في القلب عنه فإذا استولت الكلمة

rows.speaker: السهروردي
rows.claim: Al-Suhrawardī says abundant Qurʾān recitation synchronized by heart and tongue can similarly displace inner speech and make recitation and prayer easy.
rows.anchor: وقد يحصل ما ذكر بتلاوة القرآن أيضا إذا أكثر التلاوة واجتهد في مواطأة القلب مع اللسان

rows.speaker: السهروردي
rows.claim: Al-Suhrawardī compares the body to a city, its limbs to inhabitants, and the accomplished rememberer to a caller whose tongue awakens the heart and bodily parts until the heart’s light adorns the body with good works.
rows.anchor: ونقل عنه أيضا ما حاصله أن بنية العبد تحكي مدينة جامعة وأعضاؤه وجوارحه بمثابة سكان المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, those near God are annihilated and abiding through Him, established in spiritual uprightness; they have no ego-claim, glorify by negating it, and prostrate through complete self-effacement, for God alone remains.
rows.anchor: وهم الفانون الباقون به سبحانه وتعالى أرباب الإستقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports describe Sūrat al-Anfāl as Medinan, citing Zayd ibn Thābit, ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr, and a narration from Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: مدنية كما روي عن زيد بن ثابت وعبدالله بن الزبير وجاء ذلك في رواية عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Abū al-Shaykh reports that Saʿīd ibn Jubayr called it the Sūrah of Badr and, in another narration, said it was revealed at Badr.
rows.anchor: أنه سئل الحبر عنها فقال : تلك سورة بدر

rows.speaker: مقاتل وابن عباس
rows.claim: One view exempts 8:30 as Meccan, following Muqātil; al-Ālūsī rejects this because a sound report from Ibn ʿAbbās says this very verse was revealed in Medina, and finds proposed reconciliations unconvincing.
rows.anchor: إلا قوله سبحانه وتعالى : ( وإذ يمكر بك الذين كفروا ) الآية فإنها نزلت بمكة

rows.speaker: ابن العربي وابن عباس
rows.claim: Others exempt 8:64 from the Medinan surah, a view Ibn al-ʿArabī and others authenticate; al-Bazzār reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that it was revealed when ʿUmar became Muslim.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى ( يا أيها النبي حسبك الله ) الآية وصححه ابن العربي وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse counts differ: the Syrian count is 77, the Basran and Hijazi counts are 76, and the Kufan count is 75.
rows.anchor: وهي في الشامي سبع وسبعون آية وفي البصري والحجازي ست وسبعون وفي الكوفي خمس وسبعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anfāl follows the instruction to enjoin recognized good in al-Aʿrāf by detailing many instances of what is enjoined.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه كثير من أفراد المأمور به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿrāf recounts earlier prophets and their peoples, while al-Anfāl recounts the Prophet Muḥammad and what occurred between him and his people.
rows.anchor: وفي تلك ذكر قصص الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام مع أقوامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿrāf details Pharaoh and similar peoples’ destruction, while al-Anfāl summarizes their pattern in 8:52.
rows.anchor: في تلك قصص آل فرعون وأضرابهم وما حل بهم وأجمل في هذه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿrāf alludes to unbelievers’ false claim about the Qurʾān; al-Anfāl states their rejection explicitly in 8:31.
rows.anchor: هناك إلى سوء زعم الكفرة في القرآن بقوله تعالى : ( وإذ لم تأتهم بآية قالوا لولا اجتبيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After al-Aʿrāf calls the Qurʾān guidance and mercy and commands listening and remembrance, al-Anfāl describes believers whose faith grows when its verses are recited and who trust God.
rows.anchor: بالإستماع له والأمر بذكره تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the placement of al-Anfāl here, and al-Tawbah after it, is apparently divinely fixed like the placement of the other sūrahs.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن وضعها هنا توقيفي وكذا وضع براءة بعدها وهما من هذه الحيثية كسائر السور

rows.speaker: جلال السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyūṭī instead says the Prophet did not prescribe al-Anfāl’s placement for the Companions; ʿUthmān arranged it by his own reasoning.
rows.anchor: وذكر الجلال السيوطي أن ذكر هذه السورة هنا ليس بتوقيف من الرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: جلال السيوطي
rows.claim: Al-Suyūṭī says Yunus and Hūd might seem better after al-Aʿrāf because all three contain prophetic stories and are Meccan; Yunus was counted the seventh of the seven long sūrahs, so separating it by two sūrahs breaks the sequence.
rows.anchor: وذكر الجلال السيوطي أن ذكر هذه السورة هنا ليس بتوقيف من الرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās asked ʿUthmān why he joined al-Anfāl, one of the Mathānī, with al-Tawbah, one of the Miʾīn, omitted the basmala between them, and placed them among the seven long sūrahs.
rows.anchor: ما حملكم على أن عمدتم إلى الأنفال وهي من المثاني وإلى براءة وهي من المئين فقرنتم بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ālūsī begins to explain ʿUthmān’s arrangement: despite its brevity, al-Anfāl precedes al-Tawbah because it contains the basmala and can serve as its opening, while al-Tawbah completes it.
rows.anchor: الأول أنه جعل الأنفال قبل براءة مع قصرها لكونها مشتملة على البسملة فقدمها
